propositions: Duplicate CAS delivery and retry loops scattered across workflows have been consolidated into a single Python core module that owns push-first CAS retry, fetch-and-merge recovery with a five-cycle budget, and terminal push mechanics.
The new strict push mode raises typed PushDeliveryError with reason, detail, and unpushed-commit count; best-effort mode preserves backward compatibility for library, CLI, MCP, and importer callers.

Both workflow entrypoints (reconcile-bridge and reconcile-bridge-canary) now delegate delivery exactly once through Python adapters in strict mode instead of containing their own fetch/merge/retry loops.
The locked commit-and-push entrypoint stages, commits, and delivers workflow transactions atomically with established bot identity and commit subject, while preserving local commits on push failure.
Existing Python library and MCP callers retain best-effort defaults via the same public interfaces, ensuring no schema changes or breaking API modifications.
